title: Hook and first seconds
purpose: Describes exactly what happens in the first frame and the first 3-5 seconds (title, voice, motion, sound) so the opening can be rebuilt with new content.
boundary: The swarm lifts technique and structure only. Never store, transcribe or reuse the source's footage, frames, music, voice or script text. Keyframes and spectrograms are temporary analysis files in a scratch directory and are never copied into the format IR or a variant. On-screen text may be quoted only as a locating note in evidence.note, at most 6 words, and narration is never quoted. Patterns replace content words with slots, e.g. 'FACT {n}' or '{number} {unit} {noun}'. Analysing a public video for technique is fine; republishing its content is not.
inspect: F1 at 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 s; F8 over 0-0.5 s for the title entrance; A1 spectrogram over 0-3 s.
pitfalls: Reading frame 0 from a keyframe that is not at 0.0 s
Treating a platform thumbnail as the first frame
Confusing the hook line with the title text
Quoting the hook instead of turning it into a slot pattern

methods.measured: A measurement tool produced the value (an evidence.json field or an ffmpeg/ffprobe filter output). Name the tool and the field.
methods.observed: You looked at extracted frames, crops, scopes, spectrograms or waveforms and saw it. Give the timestamps you looked at.
methods.inferred: Reasoned from measured or observed facts, e.g. 'synthetic voice' from flat pitch on a spectrogram. State the reasoning in the note.
methods.assumed: No direct evidence; a default or convention. Use only for gaps the format needs filled, and keep confidence at 0.3 or lower.

pointer_conventions: ir_path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the Video format IR (contract schema video_re_format_ir).
A final '/-' means 'append this answer to the array' (the RFC 6901 end-of-array token), e.g. /motion/transitions/- or /generation_rules/-.
A '*' segment means 'each array element the answer is about'; the answer must say which elements (for example beats with role 'item'). The lifter resolves '*' to concrete indexes.
Paths under free-form objects (typography.title, typography.captions, typography.labels, audio.narration, audio.music, render_binding.mapping) use the snake_case key named in the question.

answer_types.number: {"value": n, "unit": "..."} optionally with "min" and "max"; becomes an IR observed_number
answer_types.ms: {"value": n, "unit": "ms"} optionally with "min"/"max"; signed when an offset (negative = earlier)
answer_types.enum: exactly one of the question's choices (a string)
answer_types.pattern: a template with {slots} in place of content words, e.g. 'FACT {n}: {number} {unit}'
answer_types.list: array of short strings (technique names or kinds)
answer_types.timestamps: array of seconds from the start of the source
answer_types.rule: one procedural generation rule string, at most 400 characters, written in terms of parameters
answer_types.object: a JSON object with the keys the question's how_to_answer names

recipes.F2: Burst sheet, 10 frames over 1 s: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 1 -i "$SRC" -vf "fps=10,scale=270:-2,tile=5x2" -frames:v 1 "$WORK/burst_T.jpg"
recipes.F3: Full-resolution crop (add ,scale=iw*2:-1:flags=lanczos to enlarge): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y" "$WORK/crop_T.png"
recipes.F5: Per-frame motion in a region (mean absolute frame difference, 0-255): ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -vf "crop=iw:ih*0.15:0:0,tblend=all_mode=difference,signalstats,metadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.YAVG:file=$WORK/diff.txt" -an -f null -  (drop the crop for the full frame)
recipes.F6: Per-frame colour statistics (YMIN, YAVG, YMAX, SATAVG, HUEMED, UAVG, VAVG): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t D -i "$SRC" -vf "signalstats,metadata=mode=print:file=$WORK/stats.txt" -an -f null -
recipes.F8: Every frame in a short window (animation timing; frame k is at T + k/fps): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 0.5 -i "$SRC" -vf "scale=540:-2" "$WORK/step_T_%03d.png"
recipes.F9: Average colour of a region: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y,scale=1:1:flags=area,format=rgb24" -f rawvideo - | od -An -tu1
recipes.F10: Similarity of two frames (SSIM, 1.0 = identical): ffmpeg -i a.jpg -i b.jpg -lavfi "[0:v]scale=320:-2[a];[1:v]scale=320:-2[b];[a][b]ssim" -f null - 2>&1 | grep -o "All:[0-9.]*"
recipes.F11: Per-frame scene-change score (finds dissolves and missed cuts): ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -vf "select='gte(scene,0)',metadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.scene_score:file=$WORK/scene.txt" -an -f null -
recipes.A1: Spectrogram image (add highpass=f=3000, before showspectrumpic to isolate clicks and whooshes): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t D -i "$SRC" -lavfi "showspectrumpic=s=1200x600:legend=1" "$WORK/spec_T.png"
recipes.A3: Momentary loudness every 100 ms (LUFS): ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -af "ebur128=metadata=1,ametadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.r128.M:file=$WORK/lufs_m.txt" -f null -
recipes.A5: Side (L-R) channel loudness, which removes centre-panned voice and leaves most stereo music: replace the A3 filter with "pan=mono|c0=0.5*c0-0.5*c1,ebur128=metadata=1,ametadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.r128.M:file=$WORK/side_m.txt"; mid channel uses 0.5*c0+0.5*c1. Only meaningful for stereo sources.
recipes.A6: RMS level per 100 ms at 48 kHz: ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -af "aresample=48000,asetnsamples=n=4800,astats=metadata=1:reset=1,ametadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level:file=$WORK/rms.txt" -f null -

questions.question: How many words of on-screen text are visible on the frame at exactly 0.0 s?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the first-frame title word budget (title_max_words).
questions.how_to_answer: Extract F1 at T=0 (not a keyframe from evidence, which may be later); crop the text with F3 enlarged 2x; count words without copying them beyond a 6-word locating note.
questions.challenge: Re-extract with -ss after -i (accurate seek) to rule out a seek to the wrong frame; count again.

questions.question: Where is the title's bounding box on the first frame (centre y as a fraction of height, centre x, width as a fraction of frame width)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills the title placement used by every rendered variant.
questions.how_to_answer: Use evidence.text_regions[] entries with t_s nearest 0 (bbox and y_center_ratio); confirm on F1 at 0.0 s and measure the box by pixel coordinates on a crop.
questions.challenge: Check that the region is the title and not a caption or watermark; compare the bbox with a manual measurement on the frame (tolerance 3% of height).

questions.question: Does the title overlap the main subject or photo, sit in empty space beside it, or sit on a separate band?
questions.why_it_matters: Captures whether the format layers the title over the photo (a recurring house preference) or reserves space.
questions.how_to_answer: On F1 at 0.0 s and 1.0 s, compare the title bbox with the subject region; a subject is the largest face, person or object in focus.
questions.challenge: Ask whether the 'subject' is actually a background element; if two readings are possible, lower confidence and name both.

questions.question: How many seconds after the start is the first spoken word?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the voice lead-in in the hook timing rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Read the first evidence.audio.speech_segments[0].start_s; confirm the onset on an A1 spectrogram of 0-2 s (voiced harmonics).
questions.challenge: Music with vocals can be detected as speech; check the spectrogram for a narration voice rather than sung notes.

questions.question: When is the first cut, in seconds?
questions.why_it_matters: Tells the generator how long the opening shot holds before the first visual change.
questions.how_to_answer: Take evidence.shots[0].end_s; verify with F11 scene scores over 0-5 s that no earlier dissolve or cut was missed.
questions.challenge: If the opening shot is a fast zoom, detectors may report a false cut; inspect F1 either side.

questions.question: What type of hook is used: question, bold claim, specific number, contradiction or myth, direct 'you' address, visual shock, mid-action cold open, unfinished sentence, or a promise of a list?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills hook_pattern so new videos can be written with the same opening move.
questions.how_to_answer: Read the first caption cards (evidence.captions with start_s < 5, analysis only) and the title crop; classify by the dominant move. Do not copy the line.
questions.challenge: If two types apply (number inside a question), require the note to name the secondary type and justify the primary.

questions.question: What is the hook's slot pattern with content words replaced (for example '{number} {things} that {surprising verb}')?
questions.why_it_matters: Turns the opening line into a reusable template.
questions.how_to_answer: From the first sentence (captions, analysis only) keep function words and structure, replace every noun, number, name and verb with a typed slot. Keep at most the structure, never the content.
questions.challenge: Check that no content word from the source survives in the pattern; any copied distinctive phrase is a rejection.

questions.question: Is the spoken hook the same as the on-screen title, a paraphrase of it, or different information?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether title and first line are generated together or separately.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare the title crop (F3 at 0.5 s) with the first caption/transcribed sentence; judge overlap of key content words without writing them down.
questions.challenge: Transcription errors can make a same-words title look like a paraphrase; check the audio timing alignment too.

questions.question: How many distinct visual changes (cuts, text appearances, zoom jumps, colour flashes) happen in the first 3 seconds?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the opening event density for the hook rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Count cuts (evidence.shots with start_s < 3), new text regions (text_regions t_s < 3) and visible jumps on F2 burst sheets for 0-1, 1-2, 2-3 s.
questions.challenge: Make sure a single animated title is not counted once per frame; each element counts once per appearance.

questions.question: Is there visible motion from the very first frame, or does the video open on a still?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a rule that the opening frame must already move (or may hold).
questions.how_to_answer: Use F5 (full frame) for the first 1 s and report mean frame difference; inspect F2 at 0 s.
questions.challenge: A mean difference below about 0.5 can be compression noise; verify by eye on the burst.

questions.question: How long is the silence (or near-silence) before any audio starts?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets audio lead-in; a silent first second changes autoplay behaviour.
questions.how_to_answer: Run A4 over the first 2 s and A3 momentary loudness; report ms until loudness rises above -40 LUFS.
questions.challenge: A3 momentary loudness uses a 400 ms window, so values are smeared; confirm with A6 RMS.

questions.question: Is there a sound effect (hit, whoosh, riser, pop) within the first second?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds an opening sfx slot to the audio recipe.
questions.how_to_answer: A1 spectrogram 0-1.5 s with and without highpass=f=3000; look for broadband transients or sweeps not aligned with speech; cross-check evidence.audio.onsets_s < 1.
questions.challenge: A plosive at the first word or a music downbeat is not a sound effect; the transient must stand apart from both.

questions.question: Does music start at 0 s, under the hook voice, or only after the hook ends?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills audio.music.entry for the mix recipe.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare A5 side-channel loudness (stereo) and A1 spectrogram over 0-5 s for sustained tonal or rhythmic content.
questions.challenge: Side-channel loudness is meaningless on mono audio (check A7 channels); then rely on the spectrogram and lower confidence.

questions.question: How long does the title stay on screen, and how does it leave (cut away, fade, shrink to corner, stays all video)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills title hold_s and exit behaviour.
questions.how_to_answer: Track the title region in evidence.text_regions[] from first to last t_s; inspect F8 frames around the disappearance.
questions.challenge: Check whether the 'title' that persists is actually a series tag or watermark.

questions.question: How does the title enter in its first 500 ms (pop with overshoot, scale-up, slide, type-on, fade, already present)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds the title entrance to motion.text_animations.
questions.how_to_answer: F8 frame steps over 0-0.5 s; measure the title box height per frame on the stepped images.
questions.challenge: If the title is present on frame 0 at full size, the answer must be already-present, whatever happens later.

questions.question: What colour is the title text, and what is behind it (none, solid plate, frosted blur panel, stroke, drop shadow)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills title colour and backing, both common parameters.
questions.how_to_answer: F9 average colour on a crop inside a letter stroke (choose a thick stroke, 3x3 px), and F3 crop of the backing; compare the backing region in two frames with different backgrounds to tell blur from a solid plate.
questions.challenge: Anti-aliased edges and compression shift colour; resample in two other letters and report the spread.

questions.question: How tall is the title text block relative to the frame height?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills title size_ratio for rendering at any resolution.
questions.how_to_answer: bbox height from evidence.text_regions[] near t=0 divided by source.height; for multi-line titles also report lines and per-line height from an F3 crop.
questions.challenge: A bbox that includes the backing panel overstates text size; measure letters directly on the crop.

questions.question: Does the opening show the end result or payoff first (a visual promise) before explaining it?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a 'show the payoff first' rule for the hook.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare the first shot keyframe with later keyframes using F10 SSIM; a match above 0.7 with a shot in the final third indicates a flash-forward.
questions.challenge: A shared background or template layout gives high SSIM without being the same shot; inspect the pair by eye.

questions.question: Does the first frame stay legible as a thumbnail (title readable when the frame is scaled to 20% width)?
questions.why_it_matters: Records whether the first frame doubles as the thumbnail.
questions.how_to_answer: Scale F1 at 0.0 s to 216 px wide (ffmpeg -vf scale=216:-2) and inspect whether the title words are distinguishable.
evidence_required: frames: F1 at 0.0 s scaled to 216 px
questions.challenge: Legibility is a judgement; require the note to state the scaled text height in pixels.

questions.question: What is the approximate contrast ratio between the title colour and the colour directly behind it?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets a minimum contrast constraint for generated titles.
questions.how_to_answer: Take text colour and backing colour from F9 samples; compute WCAG relative luminance contrast (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05).
evidence_required: frames: F9 text and backing samples
questions.challenge: Recompute from the reported RGB values; with a blurred photo behind the text, sample three background points and report the worst.

questions.question: Is a face visible in the first frame, and what fraction of the frame height does it occupy?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a hook framing rule (face-first or object-first).
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect F1 at 0.0 s; measure the face box height in pixels divided by frame height. Do not identify the person.
questions.challenge: Answers that name or describe the identity of a person are rejected; only size and position are allowed.

questions.question: Is the first shot shorter or longer than the video's median shot (ratio first shot / median)?
questions.why_it_matters: Tells the generator whether the hook is front-loaded with faster cuts or a longer hold.
questions.how_to_answer: evidence.shots[0].duration_s divided by evidence.shot_stats.median_s.
questions.challenge: Recompute the division; check that shot 0 is not a 1-frame black leader.

questions.question: What is the speech rate in the first 5 seconds compared with the whole video (words per minute in both)?
questions.why_it_matters: Captures whether the hook is delivered faster or slower than the body.
questions.how_to_answer: Count caption words with start_s < 5 (analysis only) divided by speech time inside 0-5 s (speech_segments); compare with evidence.audio.speech_wpm.
questions.challenge: With fewer than 8 words in the window, the rate is unstable; confidence must stay below 0.5.

questions.question: How much louder or quieter are the first 3 seconds than the integrated loudness of the whole video (dB)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets a hook loudness offset in the mix recipe.
questions.how_to_answer: Mean of A3 momentary loudness over 0-3 s minus evidence.audio.integrated_lufs.
questions.challenge: Averaging LUFS values arithmetically is approximate; note it, and check the sign against A6 RMS.

questions.question: What information is withheld by the hook (a curiosity gap), and at what timestamp is it resolved?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes an open-loop retention device with a resolution time.
questions.how_to_answer: Describe the withheld element as a slot (for example 'the identity of {item 1}'), then find where captions or labels resolve it. Give both timestamps.
questions.challenge: If the 'gap' is just the topic of the video, it is not an open loop; reject or downgrade.

questions.question: Does the hook state a specific number or quantity, on screen or in the voice?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a constraint for the hook template (must contain a number).
questions.how_to_answer: Check the title crop and first two caption cards for digits or number words; record only that a number exists and its type (count, year, measurement).
questions.challenge: Ordinals in a label (FACT 1) do not count as a hook number.

questions.question: How many seconds long is the hook segment before the body begins?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills the hook beat length.
questions.how_to_answer: Use the first non-hook beat start from structure_beats-001 or, independently, the first label appearance or first topic change; report both if they differ.
questions.challenge: Compare with the structure lens; a difference above 0.5 s must be explained in the note.

questions.question: Is a series name, recurring tag or brand mark shown in the hook?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a series_tag slot that a new format must fill with its own name.
questions.how_to_answer: Look for a small persistent text or logo region in evidence.text_regions[] near frame edges during 0-3 s; crop it with F3.
questions.challenge: Platform watermarks and usernames are not series tags; classify them for the rights lens instead.

questions.question: Is the first frame visually distinct from the rest (different grade, a frame border, a flash, a still title card)?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether frame 0 is a designed cover frame.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare F6 statistics (YAVG, SATAVG) of frame 0 against the video median; inspect F1 at 0.0 and 1.0 s.
questions.challenge: A fade-in from black makes frame 0 distinct by accident; check frames 0-5 with F8.

questions.question: Is there a zoom or punch-in on the subject during the first second, and by how much does the scale change?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds the opening camera move to motion.camera_moves.
questions.how_to_answer: Measure the width of a fixed feature on F1 at 0.0 s and at 1.0 s (same shot); ratio = later width / earlier width. Cross-check evidence.shots[0].camera.zoom.
questions.challenge: Make sure a cut did not occur between the two frames (check shots[0].end_s).

questions.question: Which hook elements are fixed format and which must become parameters (title text, title colour, hero image, hook line pattern, sound hit)?
questions.why_it_matters: Feeds the parameteriser with the hook's slots.
questions.how_to_answer: Combine answers 001-030: anything that carries content (words, image) is a parameter; style that a series would keep (placement, entrance, colour) is fixed or a parameter with a default.
questions.challenge: Each proposed parameter must point to the question that observed it (derived_from).

questions.question: Write the hook timing rule (title appear and hold, voice start, first cut, first item start) in terms of parameters.
questions.why_it_matters: Gives the compiler a reproducible opening.
questions.how_to_answer: Use measured times from 004, 005, 014 and 027, scaled where sensible (for example 'title at 0.0 s, holds title_hold_s; voice at 0.3 s; first cut at 0.8-1.2 s; first item at 0.1 x duration').
questions.challenge: Re-derive the source's opening times from the rule; any mismatch over 0.3 s must be fixed or explained.

questions.question: When does the first caption appear, and is it on screen at the same time as the title?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether captions wait for the title or overlap it.
questions.how_to_answer: First evidence.captions[] start_s (or first text region in the caption area) compared with the title hold window.
questions.challenge: If captions come from transcription (not burned in), on-screen overlap cannot be measured from them; check frames.

questions.question: Is the opening a flash-forward excerpt from later in the video (a cold-open teaser)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a teaser beat option to the format.
questions.how_to_answer: F10 SSIM of each shot in the first 3 s against all later keyframes; list matches over 0.75 with their timestamps.
questions.challenge: Matches inside the same template background are false positives; the subject must match too.

questions.question: What fraction of the frame area is covered by text during the first 3 seconds (peak)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets a text-density limit for generated hooks.
questions.how_to_answer: Max of sum(area_ratio) over evidence.text_regions[] grouped by t_s < 3.
questions.challenge: Check whether backing panels were counted as text by the detector; compare with a manual crop.

questions.question: Does the hook frame use the upper third, centre or lower third for its main text, and is the photo kept full size underneath?
questions.why_it_matters: Captures the title-over-photo layout that is cheap to get wrong in variants.
questions.how_to_answer: From title y_center_ratio (002) and the photo layer width on F1 at 0.0 s compared with its width at 3 s.
questions.challenge: Check the photo width in pixels at both times; 'photo-full' requires the same width within 5%.
